newsitem.title: UK: Firm dollar supports soft oils at Euro vegoil clos.
newsitem.headline: Firm dollar supports soft oils at Euro vegoil clos.

text.p: LONDON, April 9 - A firm dollar against major European currencies continued to support soft oils during Wednesday afternoon despite the lower opening in Chicago.
"To some extent the lower Chicago opening had been foreseen and was already in the market, but the dollar continues to dominate," said one trader.
At the close Dutch soy oil was 0.50 guilders down to unchanged while rape oil was 0.25 guilders lower to unchanged after Aug/Oct traded at 101 guilders a 100 kilos fob ex-mill
A late surge in Malaysian palm oil prices on refiner interest had little impact on a quiet sector.
Crude palm oil finished mixed at $2.50 up to $2.50 down after May fetched $550 a tonne in an outright trade and Jul/Sep traded at $545 in a switch with Jan/Mar at $540.
RBD palm oil finished a tradeless session unchanged to $2.50 up.
Olein sellers were unchanged to $2.50 at the close with no further business reported.
Coconut oil closed $5 down to unchanged after Mar/Apr traded at $725 in as switch with May/Jun at $715 and May/Jun traded at $710 in a switch with Jun/Jul at $705 a tonne cif.
Palmkernel oil sellers were unchanged after May/Jun traded at $700 in a switch with Jun/Jul at $695 a tonne.
EU origin sunflower oil fetched $545 a tonne for Jun and $567.50 a tonne for Aug ex-tank with a five ports option. --Jim Ballantyne, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8062
